say: Today we are logic inquirers. We will use clues and crosses to find an answer that is hiding. Every cross we write helps us fill in another box.
I am thinking of a number from 1 to 20. You may ask yes or no questions. Let us see how few questions we need together.
Who would like to share a question they liked? Why was it good? (“Is it more than 10?” cuts the possibilities in half.)
Here are some buttons. I will sort them into two loops that overlap. Where do you think the buttons that follow both rules will go?
stuck: Stuck: read one rule at a time. Which buttons follow rule 1?
Not sure where a button goes: “Does it follow BOTH rules? Then it goes in the middle.”
For pairs who want more: make a new rule and sort again.

say: “Tia does not drink milk. Sam does not drink milk or juice. I put a cross where it cannot be. Sam cannot have milk or juice, so Sam has water. Now Tia cannot have milk and water is taken, so Tia has juice. Raj has milk.”

“A Venn diagram: numbers 10 to 20. Less than 15 in one loop, even in the other. For each number I ask both questions. 12: less than 15? Yes. Even? Yes. So 12 goes in the middle. 16: less than 15? No. Even? Yes. So 16 goes in the even loop only.”
“Every time I write a cross I check whether it gives me a new clue.”

do: Ask: “Which box can you fill in now? What clue tells you?”
Ask: “Does this number follow both rules?”
Ask: “How do you know the answer is the only one?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Find a clue that tells you something for sure.”
Hint 2: “Put a cross where it cannot be.”
Hint 3: “Which row or column has only one box left?”

say: “Why does 12 go in the middle of the Venn diagram?”
ask: 12 is less than 15 AND even, so it follows both rules and goes where the two loops overlap.

say: “You used crosses to make a clue, and then a new clue. That is how inquirers solve puzzles.”

l8-title.note: Objective: Order things from clues, sort using two rules with a two-loop picture, solve a logic grid, and explain an odd one out. Materials: Two loops of string, buttons or small objects, clue cards. Online: Children sort objects from home by a rule shown on the slide and explain the rule on camera. Time plan: opening 0 to 2, warm-up 2 to 8 (game 2 to 6, quick questions 6 to 8; ask questions 1 to 3, and 4 and 5 only if you are on time), sneak-peek puzzles 8 to 12, explore 12 to 26, teaching 26 to 36 (click to reveal each step and answer), brain break 36 to 40, worksheet 40 to 72 with short teaching before each page and a check-together slide after it (a 30-second stand-and-stretch reset after the page-1 check, taken from that slot; the last 4 minutes check page 2, after a 1-minute stand-up stretch), talk time 72 to 79, exit ticket 79 to 85, look-back 85 to 88, then flex time and goodbye 88 to 90 (this is the buffer: if you are behind, use it; do not start anything new). Think harder, Go further and the Investigation are for every child to choose, any time or at home. Nobody is told which page they should be on. SPINE: Today's tool is Make a table. Put what you know in rows and columns. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l8-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is Make a table. Put what you know in rows and columns. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l8-warm1.note: Minutes 2 to 6. Guess my number: the tutor thinks of a number from 1 to 20. Children ask yes/no questions to find it in as few questions as they can together.

l8-warm2.note: Minutes 6 to 8. These follow on from Guess my number. Read each question aloud, give thinking time, take answers on each child's own paper (ticked against the answer slide), then click. 1) More than 10 means 11 to 20; even ones are 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. 2) Of those, less than 15: 12 and 14. Point out that each clue crosses out more numbers. 3) Counting in 5s: 5, 10, 15 (20 is not less than 20); odd: 5 and 15. 4) "Is it 7?" usually crosses out only one number. "Is it more than 10?" crosses out about half the numbers, whatever the answer. Good questions cross out lots of numbers. Ask questions 1 to 3. Ask 4 and 5 only if the clock at minute 6 is on time. The 4-minute sneak-peek puzzles follow on the next slide.

l8-warmcheck.note: Minutes 8 to 12 (4 minutes). SAY (about 26 words, once): "Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start, and I do not know is welcome. Nobody is marked." Question 1 is an access question: every child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone starts with a win. Question 2 makes you think. Children try both on their own paper (about a minute each). Then everyone answers ONCE, after the second question: face to face, each child keeps the paper low so only the tutor sees it; online, children say the answers together on three (nothing is held up to the camera). There are no private chat messages. Never use boards or paper held up in front of the group or to the camera, and never read out or compare anyone's answer. Do not write scores down or announce them. Then click to show each answer to the whole group and say "Lots of us had a different idea, and that is fine." Look for good ideas to praise in a later lesson; do not keep a list of who found question 2 easy. When the worksheet starts (minute 40) invite the WHOLE group (“When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation”), never one child by name. Everyone joins Explore and the Mini-lesson. Answers: 1) Cara. The order from shortest is Ben, Cara, Dev. 2) 15 (it is not in the 4s; it is the only odd number; it is the only one that ends in 5). Accept any reasoned answer.

l8-explore1.note: Minutes 12 to 17. Pairs work with the materials: Two loops of string, buttons or small objects, clue cards. Overlap two string loops. Sort a mixed set of buttons or objects by two rules and find the ones that belong in the middle. Online: Children sort objects from home by a rule shown on the slide and explain the rule on camera. Go further (what-if) is on this slide from the start: any pair may choose it at any time, so nobody waits. The tutor does not choose who and does not announce it. Answers: Open. Check the child can say the two rules and why the middle things follow both.

l8-explore2.note: Minutes 17 to 26. Let pairs keep working and move around the room (or breakout rooms). Gather them to answer these. Answers: 1) Red buttons with 2 holes. 2) Buttons that are not red and do not have 2 holes. 3) It holds things that follow both rules.

l8-teach1.note: Teach. Read the sentence and stress "different": no two children have the same fruit. Click 1: tick Kai and banana. Ask: "Can Kai also have the apple?" No, he has only one fruit. Click 2: cross out the rest of his row. Ask: "Can Zoe have the banana?" No, Kai has it. Click 3: cross out the rest of the column. Click 4: the why. Think-aloud: "Every time I put a tick, I get crosses for free: the rest of that row and the rest of that column. Every time I put a cross, I check whether a row or column now has only one empty box left."

l8-we1.note: Click to reveal each step; ask the group what to write before each click. Think-aloud (from the tutor script): "Tia does not drink milk. Sam does not drink milk or juice. I put a cross where it cannot be. Sam cannot have milk or juice, so Sam has water. Now Tia cannot have milk and water is taken, so Tia has juice. Raj has milk." Stress that the puzzle only works because each child drinks a DIFFERENT drink. Ask: "Which row or column has only one empty box left?" That is always the next place to look.

l8-try1.note: Children draw a 3 by 3 grid (names down the side, hats across the top) and fill it in. Click for each answer after a child explains. Lee: clue 1 crosses out red and blue, so green. Then cross out green for Kim and Max. Kim: not red (clue 2) and not green, so blue. Max: red. Check each clue again. Watch for children who stop after Lee: ask "Which row has only one empty box now?"

l8-we2.note: Click to fill each part. For every number ask two questions out loud: "Is it less than 15? Is it even?" Two yeses: the middle. One yes: that loop only. Two noes: outside. Think-aloud: "12. Is it less than 15? Yes. Is it even? Yes. Both, so it goes where the loops overlap. 16. Less than 15? No. Even? Yes. So it goes in the even loop, but not the middle. 15. Less than 15? No, it is equal to 15. Even? No. So it goes outside." Ask: "Why does 12 go in the middle?" (it follows both rules). Check: 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 11 numbers, the same as 10 to 20.

l8-try2.note: Draw the two loops on the board. Children write the answer on their own paper and say it together on three, then click. a) 15 is bigger than 10 AND we say it counting in 5s: middle. b) 5: we say it counting in 5s, but it is not bigger than 10: loop B only. c) 12 is bigger than 10, but we do not say it counting in 5s: loop A only. d) 7: neither, so outside both loops. Ask for a number that goes in the middle other than 15 (20, 25, 30 …).

l8-key.note: Say the key ideas together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Putting numbers in the middle of the two-loop picture that only fit one rule (for example 2 in the middle of "less than 6" and "odd"). (2) Giving up on the pets grid instead of using a cross to rule out. Before page 2 tell children: "Each child has a different pet." (3) Guessing a line-up without checking all the clues, or reading "behind" as "just behind". (4) In riddles, counting 20 or 40 as "between 20 and 40".

l8-break.note: Four minutes. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place.

l8-teachorder.note: Teach before worksheet page 1 (Q1 puts children, animals and ribbons in order). Draw the ladder on the board: longer at the top, shorter at the bottom. Click 1: "Longer than" means higher up. Leave a gap above and below, because more clues may come. Click 2 and 3: place each new thing next to the one it is compared with. Think-aloud: "The ruler is longer than the pencil, so the ruler goes above the pencil. The eraser is SHORTER than the crayon, so it goes below the crayon." Common mistake: writing the names in the order they appear in the clues. For heavier and lighter, or taller and shorter, use the same ladder.

l8-ws1.note: Minutes 42 to 52. Walk around. Ask "How do you know?" before giving any help. For Q2, ask pairs to say the two questions for each number: "Is it less than 6? Is it odd?" At minute 40 read questions 1 and 2 aloud, then pairs read the rest. The workbook says: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never announce who is on which page and never name a child in front of the group; invite the WHOLE group at once, for example: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Do not split a pair unless both children agree.

l8-ws1ans.note: Click each answer after a pair explains. Q1c: yellow is longer than red, red is longer than blue, blue is longer than green. Q2: check that 6 is outside (it is not less than 6, and it is even). Q2b: they follow both rules, so they go where the loops overlap. Reset (about 30 seconds, taken from this slot): when the answers are checked, everyone stands, reaches up high, shakes out their hands, takes one slow breath and sits down again, then page 2. Skip it if you are more than a minute behind.

l8-teachline.note: Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q4 is a line-up of 4 children). Draw 4 circles on the board and label the front. Think-aloud: "I start with the clue that tells me something for sure: Sue is last. Then the clue that uses Sue: just in front of Sue means right next to her, so Tom is 3rd. Kim is not first, and the only places left are 1st and 2nd, so Kim is 2nd and Raj is 1st. Now I check every clue." Teach the words: "just in front of" or "just behind" means right next to; "in front of" or "behind" means somewhere before or after, not always next to. Your turn: Cara 2nd, Ali not 1st so Ali 3rd, Ben 1st.

l8-teachriddle.note: Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q5 has one number riddle, marked "if you have time"; two more are Think harder T5). All the steps are already showing: give this slide 30 seconds. Say: "Clue 1 gives a short list. Each later clue crosses one out." Your turn: only 25 is between 20 and 30, odd and said when counting in 5s ("between" leaves out 20 and 30).

l8-teachodd.note: Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q6 asks for an odd one out and a second reason, marked "if you have time"). All the steps are already showing: give this slide 30 seconds. Say: "Three share something and one does not. 12 does not belong. A second reason: 5 has only one digit." Your turn: 13, the only odd number (also accept 10, the only one we say counting in 5s).

l8-ws2.note: Children work alone. Q3 says each child has a DIFFERENT pet: read that sentence aloud before they start; the two crosses for Clue 1 are printed. In Q4, "in front of" means somewhere in front, not always right in front. Q5 and Q6 are "if you have time"; the other two riddles are on Think harder T5. Note who may need a short catch-up next lesson.

l8-ws2ans.note: Click each answer after a child explains. Q3: Ali has no cat and no dog, so fish. Mei has no dog, and the fish is taken, so cat. Ben has the dog. Q4: Mei is 1st; Ali is in front of Ben and Ben is in front of Sam, so the order of the last three is Ali, Ben, Sam. Q5a: between 10 and 20, odd, in the 5s: 15. Think harder T5: a) 30 (20 and 40 are not between 20 and 40); b) 14 (1 + 4 = 5, less than 20). Q6: also accept "11 is the only number with 2 digits". First, everyone stands up and stretches for about a minute (reach up high, touch your toes, shake out your hands) so there is some movement before talk time.

l8-stretch.note: For any pair that chooses to try more (these are on the slide only; Think harder T1 to T4 are in the workbook). Answers: 1) Cara fish (dog or fish, not dog). Dan: not cat, not rabbit, fish taken, so dog. Ali: not cat, so rabbit. Ben: cat. 2) Eve is first. Ali is 3rd (the middle of 5), Ben 2nd, Cara 5th; 1st and 4th are left for Dan and Eve, and Dan is not first, so Dan 4th and Eve 1st: Eve, Ben, Ali, Dan, Cara. 3) 10, 20 and 30.

l8-challenge.note: For any pair that chooses Go further. Use it as a pair choice, or with volunteers in talk time (never call a child by name). Ask for the reason every time. Q3 is open: there is no single right answer, so ask children to check each other's work. Answers: 1) 12. 2) 2s and 3s: 2s only 7, 3s only 3, both 3 (6, 12, 18), neither 7. 2s and 4s: 2s only 5, 4s only 0, both 5 (4, 8, 12, 16, 20), neither 10. Every number we say counting in 4s we also say counting in 2s, so the 4s loop sits completely inside the 2s loop. 3) Open. Check by trying all 6 ways to hand out the pets. Example: Ana, Bo and Cy have a cat, a dog and a fish. Ana does not have the cat. Bo does not have the dog or the fish. Cy does not have the fish. Answer: Ana fish, Bo cat, Cy dog.

l8-chdiag.note: Show this picture slide only if a pair asks for it, or is stuck on Go further. The pictures show each problem, not its answer. Ask: What do you notice? What do we know? What do we not know yet? Can you draw or build it? Do not point out the answer; wait for a child to find a pattern.

l8-chwalk.note: Use after pairs have tried. Reveal one answer at a time and ask a child to explain before you click. Many children stop at one answer: ask "Is there another way?" and "How do you know you found them all?" For Q3, ask two pairs to swap puzzles and solve each other's.

l8-talk.note: Minutes 72 to 79. Pairs talk for 2 minutes. Then ask for volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"), never call a child by name to answer, and say that passing is always fine. No tallies and no rankings. Praise the reasons, not only the answers.

l8-exit.note: Minutes 79 to 85. Answer: Ali Extension: Create a logic grid puzzle with four friends and four pets.

l8-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 85 to 88. Start the timer (120 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
